app.name: NikTan
app.tagline: Your phone is the first checkup.
app.sub: Check your symptoms, prepare a health card and join the outpatient queue from your phone.
app.notDiagnosis: This is a screening, not a doctor's diagnosis.

landing.privacy: Your face and eye images never leave your phone.

consent.title: Before we begin
consent.onDeviceList: Face video, eye photos, vision and hearing tests
consent.uploadedList: Age, sex, pregnancy status, screening results and confirmed symptoms. Optional voice and meal photos go to speech or image providers. You can type, tap or enter dishes manually.
consent.notStoredList: Use symptoms only. Leave names, phone numbers and Aadhaar out of recordings, text and feedback.
consent.retention: Server records are cleared after 30 days by a daily cleanup. Use Delete my data on your card to erase your session earlier and clear the local copy.
consent.purpose: We use this information to prepare your screening card and show it to the hospital you choose when you join its queue.

info.title: A little about you
info.ageInvalid: Please enter an age between 0 and 120

voiceGuide.face: Hold the phone at arm’s length in even light. Keep your face inside the oval. Look straight ahead and stay still for thirty seconds.
voiceGuide.eye: In even light, look straight at the camera and take the first photo. For the second photo, gently pull down your lower eyelid, look up, and fit the red inner lid inside the box.
voiceGuide.vision: Place a card face down on the screen and match the guide to the short edge. Choose your testing distance, then cover one eye at a time. Tap the arrow that shows which way the E opens.
voiceGuide.hearing: Wear earphones in a quiet place. Check the left and right sounds first. You will hear three digits with noise. Enter the digits in the order you hear them.
voiceGuide.symptoms: Press and hold the microphone while you describe how you feel, then release it. You can also type or select symptoms. Check the list before you continue.

face.frozen: The camera image is frozen. Check the live preview or restart the scan.
face.slow: Camera frame rate is low. Close other apps and try again.
face.tracked: Tracking pulse from the highlighted skin.
face.collecting: Collecting steady frames for a pulse estimate…
face.realign: Amber regions show where tracking needs attention.
face.title: Heart rate from your face
face.instruction: Hold the phone at arm's length. Keep your face inside the circle and stay still.
face.light: Sit facing a window or light. Avoid light behind you.
face.noFace: Face not found. Move into the circle.
face.manyFaces: Keep only your face in the frame.
face.framing: Move closer so your face fills the guide.
face.lighting: Use even light across your forehead and cheeks.
face.tooDark: Too dark. Move into better light.
face.lowQuality: The reading was not clear. Try again in better light, or skip.
face.feel: Feel that? Your phone taps at your estimated heart rate.
face.stability: Reading held steady within {{n}} bpm across the scan.
face.lowConfidence: Low confidence: your pulse was found but the signal was weak, so this number is an estimate and will not change your priority. For a firmer reading, retake facing a window or bright lamp and keep very still.

eye.title: Eye check
eye.instruction: Gently pull your lower eyelid down and look up. Keep the inner red part of the eyelid in the box.
eye.align: Bring your pulled-down eyelid into the box
eye.torch: Turn on good light. Avoid coloured light.
eye.centre: Centre your eyes in the frame
eye.auto: Hold steady and it takes the photo by itself. Good, even light works best.

pallor.check: The inner eyelid looks pale, which can mean low haemoglobin. Ask for an Hb blood test; leafy greens, chana, jaggery and amla help.
pallor.normal: The inner eyelid has a healthy red colour in this photo.

jaundice.check: The white of the eye looks yellowish. This can be lighting, but yellow eyes need a doctor's check (bilirubin test).
jaundice.normal: The white of the eye does not look yellow.

cataract.check: The pupil looks cloudy or white in the light. Please see an eye doctor; cataracts are treatable.
cataract.normal: The pupil looks clear in this photo.

vision.title: Vision test
vision.calibrate: Place a bank or Aadhaar card face down on the screen. Match the guide to the short edge.
vision.distance: Hold the phone 40 cm from your eyes. Wear your usual reading glasses if you use them.
vision.coverLeft: Cover your left eye without pressing
vision.coverRight: Cover your right eye without pressing
vision.instruction: Which way are the arms of the E pointing? Swipe or tap the arrow.
vision.tooClose: Move the phone a little further
vision.tooFar: Bring the phone a little closer
vision.helper: Measure 2 m from your eyes to the phone. Wear your usual distance glasses if you use them. Ask a helper to hold the phone and enter the direction you point.
vision.resolution: This screen cannot display the test clearly at 40 cm. Try the 2 m test.
vision.dialQuestion: Look at the centre dot. Do all the lines look equally dark and sharp?
vision.contrastBanner: Both eyes open · phone at arm's length (about 40 cm)
vision.extraRefer: Some results suggest an eye test. This is a screening hint, not a diagnosis.

hearing.title: Hearing test
hearing.earphones: Put on earphones and set the volume to a comfortable level. This test uses spoken Hindi digits.
hearing.leftRight: Do you hear the sound in the correct ear?
hearing.instruction: You will hear 3 numbers with noise. Type the numbers you hear.
hearing.missing: The hearing audio stopped or could not load. You can skip this step.
hearing.experimental: Experimental Hindi hearing screening. The cutoff is provisional.
hearing.adults: This experimental hearing screening is for adults.
hearing.unable: I couldn’t hear all three digits
hearing.confirmEars: I heard each tone in the matching ear
hearing.toneOffer: One more: a tone check for each ear
hearing.toneOfferBody: About two minutes. Beeps play in one ear at a time and get quieter. Keep your earphones on and the volume where it is.
hearing.toneIntro: Tap the big button every time you hear a beep, even a very faint one.
hearing.toneListen: Listening… tap when you hear the beep
hearing.toneOk: Both ears heard the tones about equally.
hearing.toneAsym: Your two ears heard the tones differently. A proper hearing test is worth arranging.
hearing.toneDrop: High-pitched tones were harder to hear. A proper hearing test is worth arranging.
hearing.toneUnreliable: Some taps came when no beep played, so this check can't be read. You can repeat the scan later.
hearing.toneNote: Phone volume isn't calibrated, so only the difference between ears and between pitches is used. Experimental; not a diagnosis.

symptoms.title: What is troubling you?
symptoms.placeholder: e.g. fever for 3 days and cough
symptoms.micIssue: Speech could not be transcribed. You can type or select symptoms below.
symptoms.voiceNotice: Holding to speak sends a short audio clip for transcription. You can type or select symptoms below.
symptoms.browserFallback: If available, holding the microphone again uses your browser’s speech recognition service.

queue.near: Your turn is near. Please go to the counter.

thali.title: Scan your meal
thali.instruction: Photograph only the food. Choosing a photo sends it for dish recognition. You can also add dishes by hand.
thali.noFood: No food found in the photo.
thali.photoUnreadable: Couldn't open this photo. Try another photo or add dishes by hand.
thali.manual: Couldn't recognise automatically. Add dishes yourself.
thali.targetHint: Estimated portions. The bars compare this meal with one third of a reference day.
thali.defaultTarget: Without a screening profile, the comparison uses one third of a moderately active adult reference day.
thali.noDish: No dish found. Try a local name.
thali.sourceEst: Estimated from standard home recipes (ICMR-NIN IFCT 2017 values).
thali.sourceIndb: From the Indian Nutrient Databank (INDB) and ICMR-NIN IFCT 2017.

home.sub: A 3-minute screening in the browser — heart rate from your face, eyes, vision, hearing and symptoms by voice — so the OPD knows who needs care first, before you reach the counter.
home.problemTitle: Two hours in a queue for five minutes with a doctor.
home.problemBody: OPDs are first-come, first-served. A breathless patient waits behind a routine follow-up, and the doctor spends the consult asking basics nobody measured.
home.stat1: average wait in a neurology OPD
home.stat2: average consult time in the same study
home.statSource: 110.9 vs 5.3 min: a neurology OPD time-motion study; sources in the README.
home.howTitle: Five checks. One verdict. Zero guesswork.

steps.d: The camera reads tiny colour changes in your skin with every heartbeat. A signal-quality gate rejects bad light and movement.
A look at the inner eyelid flags possible anaemia; the sclera and pupil add experimental jaundice and cataract flags.
A tumbling-E chart sized to your exact screen with a bank card, one eye at a time.
Spoken Hindi digits in noise — the same method as WHO hearWHO — adaptively find your hearing threshold.
Speak in Hindi or Hinglish. Words become symptom chips you confirm. Danger signs are asked once, never assumed.

home.bentoTitle: Serious engineering behind a three-minute check.
home.b1t: Your face never leaves your phone
home.b1d: Video, eye photos, vision and hearing are processed on-device. Only numbers and flags are sent.
home.b2d: Confirmed symptoms and usable readings feed a rule engine. Voice transcription helps you enter symptoms for review.
home.b3d: Once the check is loaded, you can keep your results on the phone and sync when you reconnect.
home.b4d: Switch between English, Hindi and Chhattisgarhi, with spoken guidance during the checks.
home.b5d: Photograph your plate; nutrition from the Indian Nutrient Databank and local swaps like lal bhaji and kulthi.
home.b6d: Red-flag answers skip the queue entirely: Call 108, go to Emergency.
home.hospTitle: The OPD knows you before you arrive.
home.hospBody: A live triage board sorts every department by priority, then arrival. Doctors open a pre-consult card instead of starting from zero.
home.privBody: No name, phone number or Aadhaar is ever asked. Delete your data with one tap. Built around India's DPDP Act.
home.endSub: How are you feeling? Find out in three minutes.
home.footer: NikTan screens and prioritises. It never diagnoses. In an emergency call 108.

race.note: Illustration: 14 patients, about 6 minutes each. The breathless patient (red) arrived last.

console.chipA: Face video stays on the phone

home.consTitle: Every queue hides a sicker patient.
home.consBody: First-come, first-served treats a breathless patient like a prescription refill. NikTan surfaces the signals before the counter does.
home.hubTitle: Five checks feed one triage verdict.
home.hubBody: Each check sends numbers and flags, never images, into a versioned rule engine that sorts the queue by need, then arrival.
notifs: Pre-consult card sent to the OPD desk
home.notifBody: When a red flag appears, the board moves that patient at once. Staff see why.

found.d: POS, CHROM and OMIT pulse extraction, fused by signal quality.
Signal processing and triage rules run under automated tests.
No name, phone or Aadhaar. Delete with one tap.
Once loaded, the checks keep working on a weak network.
A lighter mode for low-memory devices keeps it smooth.

home.thaliTitle: Point your camera at lunch. See what it gives you.
home.thaliBody: Photograph your plate and NikTan names each dish, then estimates protein, iron, fibre and energy from the Indian Nutrient Databank, with swaps that grow nearby.
thaliPoints: Local swaps like lal bhaji, kulthi and ragi
home.rxTitle: Prescriptions, medicines and lab reports, made plain.
home.rxBody: One place for the paper a clinic visit leaves behind. Read a doctor's handwriting, find the Jan Aushadhi generic that costs a fraction of the brand, and see what every number on a lab report means.

assemble.title: Every check is a hero. The villain is the queue.
assemble.body: NikTan's features, each matched to the Avenger who shares its power, against the enemy every OPD patient knows.
assemble.doomBody: Victor von Doom wants to rule everything, and he is back for Avengers: Doomsday. In a public OPD he already rules: a first-come, first-served line where a breathless patient waits behind routine refills for about two hours, for five minutes with a doctor.

rx.tooLarge: This image is too large. Crop to the prescription or paste its text.
rx.reviewAdvice: The readings differ. Confirm these instructions against the original.
rx.title: Health Papers
rx.heading: Understand your prescription
rx.intro: Choose a photo or paste the wording to see the medicines, directions and follow-up instructions.
tips: Lay the paper flat in good light, the whole page in view
Hold steady so the handwriting is sharp
Medicines marked "Check" were hard to read: confirm them with the pharmacist
rx.verify: Check each one against the paper before you buy or take it.
rx.notFound: No public label was found for this name. Ask your pharmacist about it.
rx.infoError: Couldn't load medicine information. Try again later.
rx.none: No medicines could be read. Try a sharper photo of the whole prescription, or ask your pharmacist.
rx.failed: The reader is unavailable. Check your connection and try again.
rx.tooMany: Too many prescriptions read from this network. Try again in an hour.
rx.disclaimer: Reading handwriting can go wrong. Never change a dose or stop a medicine because of this page; follow your doctor and pharmacist. Medicine information comes from public US databases (NLM RxNorm, openFDA) and may differ from Indian labels. The photo is sent to an AI service to read it and is not stored.
rx.confirmLine: Ask your pharmacist to confirm this line.
rx.decode: This image could not be opened. Choose a JPEG or PNG, or paste the text.
rx.reviewPhoto: Check that the whole page is legible
rx.share: Selecting Read prescription sends this content to an AI service. You can remove personal details first.
rx.unclearLines: Lines to check with your pharmacist
rx.unrelated: This does not look like a prescription. Check the original you selected.
rx.sampleText:
Rx
1. Tab Dolo 650 — 1-0-1 × 3 days, after food
2. Tab Pan-D 40 — 1-0-0 before breakfast × 5 days
3. Tab Montair LC — 0-0-1 HS × 5 days
4. Syp Ascoril LS — 5 ml TDS × 5 days
Adv: Plenty of fluids. CBC if fever persists after 3 days. Review after 5 days.

aside.lab: Your lab report, in plain words.

saver.heading: Pay less for the same medicine
saver.intro: Photograph a strip or box. NikTan reads its ingredients and finds the Jan Aushadhi generic with the same salt and strength, at the government price.
tips: Show the side that says Composition or Each tablet contains
Keep the MRP and expiry date in view
Always ask your doctor or pharmacist before switching
saver.searchPlaceholder: Or type a salt, e.g. paracetamol 650
saver.share: Selecting Find cheaper generic sends this photo to an AI service. It is not stored.
saver.noComposition: Ingredients not visible on this side

expiry.expired: Expired ({{date}}). Do not use it; return it to a pharmacy.

saver.genericBody: Same salt from the government's Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, sold at Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
saver.typeInstead: The ingredients were not visible. Photograph the Composition side, or type the salt in the search box.
saver.noMatch: No Jan Aushadhi product with these ingredients was found. Ask the Kendra pharmacist.
saver.listPending: The Jan Aushadhi price list is being updated. Ask any Jan Aushadhi Kendra for this salt.
saver.notExact: Different strength or form: ask your doctor first
saver.unrelated: This does not look like a medicine pack. Try the side with the name and composition.
saver.failed: Couldn't check prices right now. Try again.
saver.tooMany: Too many photos from this network. Try again in an hour.
saver.disclaimer: Generic medicines with the same salt and strength work the same way, but never switch without asking your doctor or pharmacist. Prices are the government MRP and may change.

differs.ingredients: Has other salts too: not a direct swap
differs.strength: Different strength: ask your doctor first

lab.heading: Understand your lab report
lab.intro: Photograph or paste a blood, sugar, thyroid or other report. Each value is checked against the range your lab printed and explained in plain words.
tips: One page at a time, flat and in good light
Keep the reference range column in view
Your doctor reads the report together with how you feel
lab.share: Selecting Explain report sends this to an AI service. Names and IDs are left out; nothing is stored.
lab.printedFlag: Marked by the lab; the range could not be read.
lab.typicalRange: Typical adult range; your lab's range was not visible.
lab.urgent: Some values are far outside the usual range. Please show this report to a doctor today.
lab.urgentLine: Far outside the usual range: see a doctor today.
lab.unrelated: This does not look like a lab report.
lab.none: No test values could be read. Try a sharper photo.
lab.failed: The reader is unavailable. Check your connection and try again.
lab.tooMany: Too many reports from this network. Try again in an hour.
lab.disclaimer: This explains numbers; it does not diagnose. One value outside the range is often not a problem. Discuss your report with a doctor.
